// Generated by Pretzel > Data Format > Setup. It is yours to edit; regenerating asks before replacing it.
//
// This sets up DataIO for encrypted data (@@MODE_TEXT@@). The format, folder, key source and backup policy come from
// Assets/Resources/Pretzel/DataIOConfig.asset (Pretzel > Data Format). Change them there, or override them in code
// for this game start without touching the asset:
//
//     ProjectDataIO.Initialize(config => { config.saveFolder = "MyGameSaves"; });
//
// Call Initialize once from your startup code (Start or later), after the key is available, before any DataIO call.
// The key comes from the config's Key source (Keys tab): the generated PretzelDataSetup (Provider), the bundled
// JSON (BundledJson), or keys you pass yourself, for example after sign-in:
//
//     ProjectDataIO.InitializeWithKeys(keysFromYourServer);
//
// @@USAGE@@
//
// An AES key that ships with the game can be recovered by a determined player, with or without IL2CPP. This stops
// casual editing of saves and settings, not a cheater. Keep keys that must stay secret on a server.
using System;
using Pretzel.Data;
using UnityEngine;

public static class ProjectDataIO
{
    // Used only when the DataIOConfig asset is missing. The asset wins when it exists.
    private const EncryptionMode FallbackMode = EncryptionMode.@@MODE@@;
    private const KeySource FallbackKeySource = KeySource.@@KEY_SOURCE@@;
    private const string FallbackSaveFolder = "SaveData";

    private static DataIOConfig _config;
    private static DataStore _store;
    private static EncryptionKeys _clientKeys;
    private static string _description;

    public static bool IsReady => _store != null;

    /// <summary>The store behind DataIO.Default. Call Initialize first.</summary>
    public static IDataStore Store => _store ?? throw NotReady();

    /// <summary>The settings in use: a copy of the asset plus your overrides. Change them through Initialize.</summary>
    public static DataIOConfig Config => _config ? _config : throw NotReady();

    /// <summary>Which key is active and where it came from. Fingerprints only, never key material.</summary>
    public static string Describe() => _description ?? "ProjectDataIO is not initialized.";

    [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(RuntimeInitializeLoadType.SubsystemRegistration)]
    private static void ResetForPlaySession() => Shutdown();

    /// <summary>Creates the store once and installs it as DataIO.Default. Calling it again does nothing.</summary>
    /// <param name="configure">Optional overrides applied to a copy of the asset's settings.</param>
    public static void Initialize(Action<DataIOConfig> configure = null) => Create(null, configure);

    /// <summary>Same as Initialize, with keys you already have (a token flow, a key service). Keep them in memory only.</summary>
    public static void InitializeWithKeys(EncryptionKeys keys, Action<DataIOConfig> configure = null)
    {
        if (keys == null)
        {
            throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(keys));
        }

        Create(keys, configure);
    }

    /// <summary>Forgets the store and its keys and resets DataIO. Finish outstanding saves first. Also runs when Play mode starts.</summary>
    public static void Shutdown()
    {
        Release(_config);
        _config = null;
        _store = null;
        _clientKeys = null;
        _description = null;
        DataIO.Reset();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// A second store for other data, such as settings or a cache. It starts from the same settings and keys in its own folder
    /// under the persistent data path, and you can override anything for this store only. Create it once and keep it.
    /// </summary>
    public static DataStore CreateStore(string subFolder, Action<DataIOConfig> configure = null)
    {
        DataIOConfig copy = UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(Config);
        try
        {
            configure?.Invoke(copy);
            return copy.CreateStore(DataRoots.PersistentData(subFolder), copy.format == DataFormat.Encrypted ? _clientKeys : null);
        }
        finally
        {
            Release(copy);
        }
    }
//@@IF_RSA
    /// <summary>
    /// For a TRUSTED SERVER or tool that holds the RSA private key: reads the files a game wrote with the public key.
    /// Never call this in a shipped game, and never ship the private key.
    /// </summary>
    public static DataStore CreateServerStore(string receivedFolder, EncryptionKeys serverKeys)
    {
        if (serverKeys == null || !serverKeys.HasPrivateKey)
        {
            throw new ArgumentException("The server needs its RSA private key.", nameof(serverKeys));
        }

        DataIOConfig copy = CreateConfig(null);
        try
        {
            copy.format = DataFormat.Encrypted;
            copy.encryptionMode = EncryptionMode.Rsa;
            return copy.CreateStore(DataRoots.Absolute(receivedFolder), new EncryptionKeys { RsaPrivateKey = serverKeys.RsaPrivateKey });
        }
        finally
        {
            Release(copy);
        }
    }
//@@END_IF
    private static void Create(EncryptionKeys given, Action<DataIOConfig> configure)
    {
        if (IsReady)
        {
            if (configure != null || given != null)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("ProjectDataIO is already initialized. Call Shutdown first to apply different settings or keys.");
            }

            return;
        }

        DataIOConfig config = CreateConfig(configure);
        DataStore store;
        EncryptionKeys clientKeys;
        string description;
        try
        {
            if (config.format != DataFormat.Encrypted)
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException("The DataIOConfig is not set to Encrypted, but this setup is for encrypted data. "
                    + "Choose Encrypted on the Format tab, or generate the plain, GZip or BSON setup on the Setup tab.");
            }

            string origin = "keys passed to InitializeWithKeys";
            EncryptionKeys keys = given ?? EncryptionKeys.Resolve(config.environmentPrefix, config.keySource, out origin);
            if (keys == null || !keys.CanWrite(config.encryptionMode))
            {
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"No {config.encryptionMode} key was found (key source: {config.keySource}). "
                    + "Export the key on the Keys tab and make the key source match it, or pass keys to InitializeWithKeys.");
            }

            // A game client only ever holds what it needs: the AES key, or just the RSA public key.
            clientKeys = keys.ForClient(config.encryptionMode);
            store = config.CreateStore(null, clientKeys);
            description = clientKeys.Describe(config.encryptionMode, origin);
        }
        catch
        {
            Release(config);
            throw;
        }

        _config = config;
        _store = store;
        _clientKeys = clientKeys;
        _description = description;
        DataIO.Default = store;
        Debug.Log("[ProjectDataIO] Ready. " + description);
    }

    private static DataIOConfig CreateConfig(Action<DataIOConfig> configure)
    {
        DataIOConfig asset = DataIOConfig.Load();
        DataIOConfig config = asset ? UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(asset) : ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<DataIOConfig>();
        if (!asset)
        {
            config.format = DataFormat.Encrypted;
            config.fileExtension = DataFormats.DefaultExtension(DataFormat.Encrypted);
            config.encryptionMode = FallbackMode;
            config.keySource = FallbackKeySource;
            config.saveFolder = FallbackSaveFolder;
        }

        try
        {
            configure?.Invoke(config);
        }
        catch
        {
            Release(config);
            throw;
        }

        return config;
    }

    private static void Release(DataIOConfig config)
    {
        if (!config)
        {
            return;
        }

        if (Application.isPlaying)
        {
            UnityEngine.Object.Destroy(config);
        }
        else
        {
            UnityEngine.Object.DestroyImmediate(config);
        }
    }

    private static InvalidOperationException NotReady()
    {
        return new InvalidOperationException("Call ProjectDataIO.Initialize() from your startup code before using DataIO.");
    }
}
